questions_visited.archetype: Direct calculation from constant horizontal velocity
questions_visited.why_selected: Shows that the first representation choice isolates horizontal constant-velocity motion before calculation.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Find time from horizontal displacement and constant horizontal velocity.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Identify no horizontal acceleration, then use the constant-velocity relationship with matching time for the vertical motion.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Mixing horizontal range with vertical free-fall values before finding the shared time.
lesson_sections_informed: Start by asking what the question needs

questions_visited.why_selected: Shows that one situation can need a constant-velocity equation followed by a vertical constant-acceleration equation.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Use known horizontal time to calculate vertical drop.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Switch deliberately from horizontal constant velocity to vertical free fall with zero initial vertical velocity.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using the horizontal velocity as the initial vertical velocity.
lesson_sections_informed: When an equation is the shortest route
A representation must agree with the motion

questions_visited.why_selected: Provides the time-free maximum-height route used to teach choice of an equation that avoids an unnecessary unknown.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Use the zero vertical velocity at maximum height with constant acceleration.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Take upward as positive, set final vertical velocity to zero, and apply the time-free equation.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Treating acceleration due to gravity as positive after choosing upward as positive.
lesson_sections_informed: When an equation is the shortest route

questions_visited.why_selected: Shows words, resolved components, equations and a resultant-displacement geometry check in one whole-question context.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Find time to maximum height, horizontal displacement, then resultant displacement magnitude.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Resolve velocity, find time vertically, find horizontal displacement, then combine perpendicular displacement components.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Calling the curved flight path the displacement from launch to the highest point.
lesson_sections_informed: A representation must agree with the motion

questions_visited.why_selected: Tests the graphical evidence for constant acceleration rather than a numerical calculation.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Identify a straight line with constant gradient on a velocity-time graph.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Name the gradient as acceleration and connect constant gradient with constant acceleration.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Describing a straight graph as constant velocity without checking that the vertical axis is velocity.
lesson_sections_informed: When a graph is the shortest route

questions_visited.why_selected: Requires separate positive and negative velocity-time areas before interpreting the initial height.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Calculate and combine signed displacements from two triangles.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Split at zero velocity, calculate upward and downward signed areas, then use the physical position relation.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Adding all areas as positive distance when the question needs displacement and height.
lesson_sections_informed: When a graph is the shortest route

questions_visited.why_selected: Requires a graph shape, not a calculated number, and distinguishes distance-time gradient from velocity-time gradient.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Sketch an increasing curve whose gradient decreases to zero.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Connect distance-time gradient to speed and slowing upward motion to a flattening curve.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Drawing a downward distance-time graph because the object is slowing down.
lesson_sections_informed: When a graph is the shortest route
